v4.9.076 - a sync leaves the shooting order alone, and a strip stops breeding versions (#357, #358)

#357 A PULL DOES NOT CLOSE THE SHOOTING ORDER YOU ARE IN.

     Every pull that rebuilt closed the sort-edit view first, and the rebuild
     also cleared WHICH order was open. Being thrown out of an order leaves 3x2
     underneath - so making a group, naming a break or moving a break pushed,
     pulled, and dropped Roman into 3x2. He reported it three times in three
     different words and I guessed at it four times before this.

     #352 had kept the sort view switched ON but left "which one" behind, which
     leaves exactly the same hole.

     The order is now kept and REDRAWN after the rebuild, because the frames it
     lists are new objects. The five places that really do replace the project -
     opening another project, logging out, deleting the account, starting a new
     one, restoring a snapshot - still close it, correctly.

     Two wrong attempts on the way, both caught by the test rather than by Roman:
     removing only the close call (the rebuild still cleared which one), then
     keeping it only if the order still existed (at that moment it cannot -
     shooting orders arrive as per-item settings applied further down, so the
     check read an empty list and threw the order away every time).

#358 LOOKING AT A STRIP MUST NOT MAKE A VERSION.

     Showing a strip makes an empty placeholder version on every frame so the
     card has something to draw. Nobody made it - but it was sent to the server
     like any other version, with a name of its own. So the desktop looked at the
     REFS strip and put 29 empty versions up there; the iPad looked at the same
     strip and put up 29 more. Both devices then showed two tabs on every card,
     both reading "r1", and neither had made a single one of them. Tagging frames
     with a setup is what carried them up: a tagged frame is unsent work, and
     unsent work takes the protective branch of the pull, which keeps the local
     copy and adds the cloud's alongside.

     Two halves, both needed:
       - a strip nobody has touched sends nothing
       - and when a real version arrives, the blank one steps aside instead of
         sitting next to it

     Deliberately narrow: a stroke, a picture, a note, a star, a setup tag, a
     hidden flag or a second version all make it work, and work is always sent
     and always kept. Anything that has ever reached the server keeps its name,
     so nothing that exists anywhere can be dropped by this.

     It stops new ones. The empty versions already on the server stay until
     somebody removes them; the app does not delete versions on its own.

THE SIMULATOR

New doors: open a shooting order, ask which one is open, look at a strip, read
the version tabs. Two new tests, both written before either fix and both failing
first, for the right reasons.

Still open and now reproducible: a random day with seed 985927 ends with the two
devices disagreeing - one frame carrying older writing, and the frames in a
different order - after the tablet was away while the desktop rearranged twice.
Same ending every replay, so it is real. Next hunt.
